strategy.thesis: Asia's first sports-technology innovation accelerator, building Taiwan into an Asia-Pacific sports-innovation hub by connecting sports-tech startups with corporates, sports bodies and APEC-economy networks.

program.location: IAPS, National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University, Hsinchu

summary.en: ASPN Sports Tech Accelerator (originally launched in 2018-2019 as HYPE Global Virtual Accelerator Taiwan / SPIN Accelerator Taiwan) is Asia's first sports-technology accelerator. Guided by Taiwan's Ministry of Education Sports Administration and executed by NYCU's IAPS — initially in partnership with Israel's HYPE Sports Innovation, and since Oct 2023 with the APEC Sport Policy Network (ASPN) of 11 Asia-Pacific economies — it has cultivated 130+ startups from 25 countries and helped them generate over NT$1 billion (~US$33M) in investment outcomes. Partners include Foxconn, Decathlon, MySports, NVIDIA and Plug and Play.
summary.local: ASPN 運動科技加速器（2018-2019 年以 HYPE GVA Taiwan / 運動創新加速器之名啟動）為亞洲第一個運動科技加速器，由教育部體育署指導、陽明交大 IAPS 執行，初期與以色列 HYPE Sports Innovation 合作，2023 年 10 月起改與 APEC 運動政策網絡（ASPN，11 個亞太經濟體）合作。

summary.en: S2B (Startups To Business) is a Taichung-based vertical accelerator run since 2018 by the non-profit Footwear & Recreation Technology R&D Center (財團法人鞋類暨運動休閒科技研發中心). It focuses on three life-technology verticals — footwear, sports & fitness, and assistive technology — across materials, sensing, manufacturing, IoT and AI. The center has recruited and mentored 100+ startup teams and connects them with ASEAN/India buyer delegations; the 2025 bootcamp ran Aug-Sep with NT$60,000/NT$30,000 awards and no equity.

summary.en: Systex AGP (AI+ Generator Program / AI+新創加乘器計畫) is a non-profit, no-equity corporate accelerator run since 2018 by Taiwanese IT-services giant Systex. Unlike typical corporate accelerators it does not take equity or run generic fundraising/pitch training; instead it targets AI startups with validated, scalable products and connects them to Systex's ~40,000 enterprise clients for industry landing and global expansion. Over 7 years it has selected 52 startups; its 8th cohort (2025) picked 7 teams.

summary.en: CnC Club (仙人掌俱樂部 / Cactus Club), founded 2018 in Taipei's Neihu, is an 'atypical' market-oriented accelerator for small and young startups that builds co-creation networks bridging founders ('Cactus') and corporate mentors ('Coach'). summary.en: CDIB Innovation Accelerator (中華開發創新加速器), established 3 Aug 2017 by CDIB Capital (中華開發金控), pioneered Taiwan's first 'invest first, then accelerate' model. It assembled a heavyweight mentor group led by internet entrepreneur 詹宏志 (Jan Hung-tze) and publisher 何飛鵬, with corporate partners Quanta, Advantech, Catcher and FarEasTone providing practical advisory on patents, organization and operations. Related: CDIB later opened a Tokyo node (2023) and a Taiwan-Japan cross-border innovation accelerator/fund.

summary.en: CDIB's Taiwan-Japan cross-border innovation accelerator opened its Tokyo node in March 2023 as a 'home' for portfolio startups expanding into Japan. In 2024 CDIB and Japan's Cool Japan Fund co-set up CDIB Cross Border Innovation Ltd to raise a US$75-100M fund (CDIB Cross Border Innovation Fund II), backed by Taiwan's NDF, Cool Japan Fund and Taiwan industry (Himax, Systex). Within five months it invested ~US$5M in 3 startups (Redcliff, Aiello, AlleyPin).

summary.en: Rocketindo (印尼火箭), founded 2016 by Daniel Liu and registered in Taiwan's FINDIT cluster review as an accelerator, is positioned as an 'Indonesia cross-border e-commerce accelerator.' summary.en: The Asia UAV AI Innovation Application R&D Center (亞創中心), inaugurated 13 Aug 2022 in Puzih, Chiayi County (on the renovated former NTU Sport Chiayi campus), is the core base of Taiwan's drone industry cluster and a vertical incubation hub for UAV/drone startups. summary.en: The Taiwan Startup Institute (TSI / 產學研鏈結中心) is a national-level deep-tech accelerator established in 2017 under the Ministry of Science and Technology's 'Value Creation Program' (價創計畫) and headquartered at Taipei Tech. It uncovers promising university/research-institute R&D and guides it toward commercialization, offering each team phased startup grants of up to NT$50 million plus legal, IP, market, financial and equity-planning support. It has trained 100+ teams, with 20+ raising a cumulative NT$2 billion (some secondary reports cite NT$2.75 billion across 28 startups).
summary.local: Taiwan Startup Institute（TSI／產學研鏈結中心）2017 年成立於台北科技大學，是科技部『價創計畫』下的國家級深科技加速器，挖掘大學與研究機構研發成果並推動商業化，每隊可獲分階段最高新台幣 5,000 萬元創業補助，已輔導逾百隊。
